definitions.explanation: A small, tucked-away corner or section of a larger space. Often implies a quiet, inconspicuous, or marginal location. Used both literally for physical spaces and figuratively for peripheral areas of larger domains.

examples.japanese: {部屋|へや}の{片隅|かたすみ}に{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: I sat in a corner of the room.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}の{片隅|かたすみ}に{小|ちい}さな{花|はな}が{咲|さ}いていた。
examples.english: Small flowers were blooming in a corner of the garden.

examples.japanese: この{世界|せかい}の{片隅|かたすみ}で{静|しず}かに{暮|く}らしたいと{思|おも}うことがある。
examples.english: Sometimes I think I'd like to live quietly in a corner of this world.

notes:
USAGE:
Often preceded by a location + の: {部屋|へや}の{片隅|かたすみ} (a corner of the room), {街|まち}の{片隅|かたすみ} (a corner of the city). Carries a nuance of being small, quiet, or overlooked, unlike {角|かど} (a geometric corner) or {隅|すみ} (a corner of a room). The phrase {世界|せかい}の{片隅|かたすみ} (a corner of the world) was popularized by the animated film of the same title.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {心|こころ}の{片隅|かたすみ}: a corner of one's heart
- {世界|せかい}の{片隅|かたすみ}: a corner of the world
- {記憶|きおく}の{片隅|かたすみ}: a corner of one's memory
- {街|まち}の{片隅|かたすみ}: a nook of the city
